thought.text: Let me verify the admin password properly using Devise's class method:

reasoning_content:
The runner's multi-line parsing got broken again (a quoting issue with `puts ... ? true : false` and quotes). The user was found (admin exists with the document_number seed value). `authenticate` doesn't exist as an instance method on the User model (it's Devise's `active_for_authentication?` / `valid_password?` / `Devise`... actually, in Devise, `authenticate` is at the model class level: `User.authenticate`... no wait. Devise's `valid_password?` is a class method. The instance method is `valid_password?(password)`. Let me use `User.valid_password?("Aa12345678")` — hmm, that's also a class method: `User.valid_password?('Aa12345678')` checks by email address. Let me use that together with the email address.

Also, an important point: `db/seeds.rb` uses the new terms field (terms_data_storage, etc.) — this is the fork's canonical production seed. This further corroborates that the fork migrated to the new terms field, and it's dev_seeds that's the old one.

action.command: cd /workspace && export PATH=/usr/local/ruby/bin:$PATH PGPASSWORD=root && timeout 200 bin/rails runner 'puts "admin valid_password: " + User.valid_password?("admin@consul.dev", "Aa12345678").to_s; puts "role users: " + %w[mod@consul.dev manager@consul.dev valuator@consul.dev verified@consul.dev unverified@consul.dev].map { |e| e.split("@").first + "=" + User.where(email: e).count.to_s }.join(", ")' 2>&1 | tail -4
